```{r}
library(icorp26)
library(easystats)
library(ggplot2)
```


The raw data is located here:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elinw/icorp26/refs/heads/main/data-raw/juan/battle-assignment1-data.csv

Copy that url and go look at the data.

You can read the data from the URL directly into
an R dataset.

```{r}
mydata <- read.csv(
     "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elinw/icorp26/refs/heads/main/data-raw/juan/battle-assignment1-data.csv"
)
```
Let's see what the data look like.

```{r}
mydata
```
*Question: How are the variable names different 
from what you see on the url?*


Notice that each row represents 1 person and 
each column represents one variable.

You can also type

View(mydata) to see the data on a tab.

If you look in the "Environment" tab on the 
top right window you should see mydata listed.

You can get a quick summary of the dataset.

```{r}
report(mydata)
```

Let's make frequency tables.

Here's an example for gender.
```{r}
data_tabulate(mydata$Gender)
```
